question: What is the primary clinical goal when initially encountering a patient presenting with an animal bite or insect sting?

options.A: Obtaining a detailed socio-economic and occupational history
options.B: Suturing the wound tightly to prevent further environmental exposure
options.C: Rapid recognition of life threats and systematic prioritization of care

explanation: Initial management of any acute trauma focuses on stabilization, identifying life-threatening systemic reactions, and prioritizing immediate resuscitation needs. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T6#GNS112_U7_T6_h1)

question: Why do bite and sting presentations vary so significantly between rural farming populations and urban residents in regions like West Africa?

options.A: Genetic resistance to local venoms developed by urban populations over generations
options.B: Differences in human immune system baseline function across climates
options.C: Disparities in standard surgical training among primary healthcare nurses
options.D: Variations in local fauna distribution, occupational hazards, and environmental exposure

explanation: Geographic location dictates the specific types of venomous snakes, spiders, and stinging insects that humans encounter during daily activities like farming or walking outdoors. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T6#GNS112_U7_T6_h1)

question: Which category of venom primarily targets the neuromuscular junction to cause paralysis and respiratory compromise?
explanation: Neurotoxins disrupt nerve impulse transmission, frequently resulting in descending paralysis and respiratory muscle failure if left untreated. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T6#GNS112_U7_T6_h2)

question: A patient bitten by a viper exhibits severe localized swelling, blistering, and active bleeding from venipuncture sites. What primary mechanism explains these clinical findings?

options.A: Direct destruction of red blood cell membranes by local neurotoxins
options.B: Systemic blockade of acetylcholine receptors at motor endplates
options.C: Immediate IgE-mediated histamine release causing bronchial smooth muscle spasm
options.D: Disruption of the normal coagulation cascade and localized tissue necrosis

explanation: Viper venoms typically contain hemotoxins and cytotoxins that provoke local tissue breakdown and systemic bleeding disorders. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T6#GNS112_U7_T6_h2)

question: What is the primary purpose of marking the leading edge of edema with a pen alongside the time following a snakebite?

options.A: To track the rate of local venom spread and tissue swelling over time
options.B: To calculate the exact dosage of prophylactic antibiotics required
options.C: To prevent the migration of neurotoxins into the central circulation
options.D: To map out the exact surgical incision lines for future debridement

explanation: Drawing a border around swelling with a timestamp allows healthcare providers to objectively evaluate whether local tissue injury is rapidly advancing. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T6#GNS112_U7_T6_h3)

question: Which finding during the primary survey of a patient stung by multiple wasps requires the most urgent nursing intervention?

options.A: Localized numbness radiating slightly up the affected forearm
options.B: Audible stridor, wheezing, and rapid development of facial edema
options.C: Anxiety and mild tachycardia due to acute fright from the attack
options.D: Mild localized erythema and throbbing pain at the sting sites

explanation: Stridor, wheezing, and facial swelling indicate impending airway obstruction from anaphylaxis, which takes precedence over local pain. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T6#GNS112_U7_T6_h3)

question: Why is scraping a honeybee stinger off the skin preferred over using tweezers to pull it out?

options.A: Scraping stimulates local immune cells to neutralize remaining toxins
options.B: Scraping prevents the complete removal of the venom apparatus from the skin
options.C: Squeezing with tweezers can empty the remaining venom sac into the wound
options.D: Tweezers frequently break the stinger and cause deep subcutaneous splinters

explanation: Pinching a honeybee stinger squeezes the attached venom reservoir, forcing additional toxin directly into the subcutaneous tissue. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T6#GNS112_U7_T6_h4)

question: A patient arrives at the clinic with a localized bee sting on the hand, complaining of intense burning pain and swelling. Which nursing action is most appropriate?

options.A: Immersing the entire hand in hot water to denature the remaining insect proteins
options.B: Scraping the stinger away, applying a cold pack, and elevating the hand
options.C: Applying a tight arterial tourniquet above the elbow of the affected arm
options.D: Administering intravenous epinephrine immediately as a preventative measure

explanation: Standard conservative management for localized stings involves stinger removal, cold therapy to reduce swelling and pain, and elevation. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T6#GNS112_U7_T6_h4)

question: Which traditional first-aid practice for snakebites is currently recognized as dangerous and strictly contraindicated?

options.A: Making cross-cut incisions over the fang marks and applying oral suction
options.B: Keeping the patient calm and immobilizing the affected limb
options.C: Gently washing the bite area with soap and clean water
options.D: Transporting the victim rapidly to a designated healthcare facility

explanation: Incisions and suction do not remove significant venom, but they frequently cause severe local hemorrhage, nerve damage, and secondary infection. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T6#GNS112_U7_T6_h5)

question: What is the primary rationale for performing copious high-pressure irrigation on a deep dog bite wound during initial nursing care?

options.A: To stimulate local vasoconstriction and stop bleeding from severed capillaries
options.B: To flush out bacteria, saliva, and foreign debris to minimize infection risk
options.C: To numb the nerve endings surrounding the bite site before suturing
options.D: To dilute any residual animal saliva toxins remaining in the subcutaneous space

explanation: Animal bites introduce heavy bacterial loads from oral flora deep into tissues, making mechanical irrigation essential to prevent infection. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T6#GNS112_U7_T6_h5)

question: What is the absolute first-line pharmacological intervention for a patient experiencing acute anaphylactic shock following an insect sting?
explanation: Epinephrine is the critical life-saving drug in anaphylaxis, reversing vasodilation, bronchial constriction, and mucosal edema rapidly. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T6#GNS112_U7_T6_h6)

question: Which set of clinical signs best confirms the progression of a local insect sting into systemic anaphylaxis?

options.A: Urticaria, wheezing, facial swelling, and sudden drop in blood pressure
options.B: Localized pain, slight erythema, and mild swelling confined to the wrist
options.C: Localized numbness, tingling, and a dull ache radiating up the arm
options.D: Fever, chills, purulent drainage, and regional lymph node tenderness

explanation: Anaphylaxis is characterized by the involvement of multiple organ systems, notably skin manifestations paired with respiratory compromise and cardiovascular instability. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T6#GNS112_U7_T6_h6)

question: What is a major physiological concern when treating deep, puncture-type animal bites on the hands or feet?

options.A: High risk of rapid systemic dehydration and electrolyte imbalance
options.B: Immediate development of chronic systemic hypertension
options.C: Permanent loss of visual acuity within the first twenty-four hours
options.D: High susceptibility to deep tissue infections and compartment syndrome

explanation: Puncture wounds seal bacteria deep within confined fascial spaces, making them exceptionally difficult to clean and prone to serious deep infections. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T6#GNS112_U7_T6_h7)

question: A patient admitted two days ago for a severe snakebite on the lower leg now complains of unremitting pain that worsens with passive toe movement, alongside pale, cool toes. What condition should the nurse suspect?

options.B: Developing compartment syndrome from localized edema
options.C: Anaphylactic shock secondary to antivenom administration
options.D: Generalized viral gastroenteritis acquired in the ward

explanation: Pain out of proportion, pain on passive stretch, and pulselessness or pallor in an extremity indicate increasing pressure within unyielding fascial compartments. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T6#GNS112_U7_T6_h7)

question: What is an essential self-care device that patients with a known severe allergy to insect stings must be taught to carry at all times?

options.B: A bottle of broad-spectrum antibiotic capsules

explanation: Carrying an epinephrine autoinjector allows individuals experiencing sudden anaphylaxis to administer life-saving medication before reaching a clinical facility. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T6#GNS112_U7_T6_h8)

question: Which advice is most appropriate for a farmer living in a rural Nigerian community to minimize the risk of nocturnal snakebites around the homestead?

options.A: Clearing brush, elevating firewood, and using mosquito nets or bed raised off the floor
options.B: Leaving outdoor lights switched off to avoid attracting venomous insects
options.C: Sleeping directly on the bare earthen floor to stay cool during hot nights
options.D: Applying herbal tourniquets preemptively around both ankles before going to sleep

explanation: Reducing nesting habitats around living quarters and sleeping above ground level significantly decreases accidental nocturnal encounters with snakes. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T6#GNS112_U7_T6_h8)
